title: Callback
description: An outbound HTTP request contract attached to an operation, in which the API itself calls a consumer-supplied URL. The URL is obtained by evaluating a runtime expression against the triggering request or response, and the full interaction (method, body, expected responses) is described as a PathItem. Use Operation instead when the HTTP interaction is one the API receives and serves on its own paths, rather than a request the API sends to a URL supplied by the consumer. Use Link instead when the relationship describes a follow-up call that the client makes to another operation of this API, using values from a response, rather than a call the API pushes to the client. Use PathItem instead when modelling the set of HTTP methods under a fixed path template of the API, or the inner PathItem that a callback aggregates, rather than the expression-keyed callback wrapper. Use Server instead when the target is a fixed or variable-templated deployment base URL of the API, not a URL resolved per request from a runtime expression.

expression.description: OpenAPI 3.0 Runtime Expression (e.g., $request.body#/callbackUrl) resolved at runtime against the triggering request to determine the callback target URL.

x-dr-evidence: A 'callbacks:' map under an operation in an OpenAPI YAML/JSON file whose keys are runtime expressions such as '{$request.body#/callbackUrl}'.
A route decorator or annotation declaring callbacks, such as FastAPI's callbacks= router parameter or springdoc/Swagger @Callback, on a subscription or job-submission endpoint.
Handler code that stores a callbackUrl/notifyUrl field from the incoming request and later issues an HTTP POST to it from a background job or event listener using an HTTP client.
